maya: Quick FYI — I'm opening a docs PR to resample the SDK snippets in the Optimize toolkit section. Specifically: batching examples, prefix caching note, and a clearer quantization profile migration note. PR coming in ~10m.

maya: Link to draft (will update once PR is up): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/ — placeholder for now.

tony: Thanks — is this targeting the quickstart or the deeper tuning guide?

maya: Targeting both. Quickstart will get a compact example (easy drop-in). Tuning guide gets the full migration checklist and rationale for profile choices.

liam: Can you add the minimal SDK snippet for batched calls? We keep getting support tickets where customers send sequential calls instead of batching. Small example helps.

maya: Yep, added a small Python + JS snippet in the draft. Python:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
# batch_size controls how many prompts we send in a single request
prompts = ["Summarize: ...", "Summarize: ..."]
resp = client.generate(model="rw1-quant-v2", prompts=prompts, max_tokens=120, batch_size=2)
print(resp.texts)
```

maya: JS snippet:
```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood()
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw1-quant-v2', prompts: ['A','B'], max_tokens: 120, batch_size: 2 })
console.log(resp.outputs)
```

emily: LGTM. Two asks: 1) add a sentence explaining when to prefer batching vs streaming (latency tradeoff), and 2) fix the broken anchor on quant profiles -> we had that link moved last week.

maya: Good catch on the link — I found the new anchor: https://docs.redwood.ai/optimize/quantization#profile-compatibility — will update.

docs-bot: [link-check] Detected 1 broken link in optimize/batching.md -> replaced with /optimize/quantization#profile-compatibility (auto-suggest).

tony: For the migration checklist, suggest a tiny decision tree:
- if cost is the priority -> start with int8 profile A
- if quality is priority -> use int8+KV or fp16 fallback
- if you have heavy caching -> allow aggressive quant and validate on prompt set

liam: Also include the quick eval snippet that runs a prompt set against new profile and compares Rouge/BLEU or token-perf metrics. That helped Sales avoid regressions last quarter.

maya: Adding a lightweight eval snippet (python) that posts counts + avg latency:
```python
from redwood import Client
import time
client = Client(model='rw1-quant-v3')
prompts = open('eval_prompts.txt').read().splitlines()
latencies = []
for p in prompts:
    t0 = time.time()
    resp = client.generate(prompt=p, max_tokens=50)
    latencies.append(time.time()-t0)
print('avg_latency', sum(latencies)/len(latencies))
```

emily: Nice. Could we also show a tiny sample output that highlights when tokenization differences matter? A one-liner explaining "if generation deviates > X% on key metric, roll back or try fp16".

maya: Adding: "If your eval shows >3% quality regression on the chosen metric, revert and try the fp16 fallback or narrower quant profile." Will include in the checklist.

tony: Also add a short note about KV cache compatibility for quantized models — some older kernels needed the cache warmup tweak. Include the command snippet we used in ops:
```bash
# warm up KV cache with an example prefix to stabilize latency
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rw1-quant-v3","prompt":"Warmup: hello","max_tokens":1}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

liam: One more: update the SDK doc reference in the header so customers can find the code samples from the console (we should not duplicate sample text vs console quickstart). Maybe add a "See also" link.

maya: Will add a "See also: SDK quickstart" link and cross-ref to the console examples.
